newsitem.title: BERMUDA: EXEL Q1 premiums fall due to reinsurance.
newsitem.headline: EXEL Q1 premiums fall due to reinsurance.

text.p: EXEL Ltd said premiums in the first quarter of 1997 were sharply reduced by the impact of certain specialty reinsurance assumed contracts written a year ago, which were canceled and rewritten.
EXEL said the cancellation and reissue of these programs began in the third quarter of 1996 and has no impact on the earnings of the company.
Net premiums written fell to about $77 million in the first quarter from about $164 million in the year ago quarter.
EXEL also reported first quarter operating earnings of $0.86 a share, about in line with the First Call consensus.
The First Call consensus was $0.85 a share. EXEL reported first quarter operating earnings of $0.74 a share a year ago.

EXEL said that after adjustment for multi-year premiums and the volatility caused by the specialty reinsurance assumed contracts, net premiums written in the first quarter of 1997 were $105.1 million compared with $130.8 million in 1996.
Although competition pressured its general liability business, EXEL chief executive Brian O'Hara said the company's other insurance product lines posted premium growth in the 1997 first quarter.
He said the company's Employment Practices Liability and X.L. Risk Solutions, its two newest areas of operation, had strong performances in the quarter.
EXEL said its combined ratio in the 1997 first quarter was 88.8 percent compared with 93.6 percent in the year ago quarter.

The improved combined ratio reflects a decline in the loss and loss expense ratio, stemming from the release of redundant short-tail reserves -- or reserves for the kinds of business for which claims would be made quickly -- and the release of reserves relating to the cancellation of the specialty reinsurance assumed contracts.
However, the underwriting expense ratio increased, reflecting the lower premium base resulting from the reduction in specialty reinsurance assumed premiums as well as higher acquisition expenses.

EXEL also said that in the first quarter of 1997, the company earned $13.2 million from its equity in the net earnings of its affiliate, Mid Ocean Ltd, compared with $16.1 million in the first quarter of 1996.
At February 28, 1997 EXEL owned approximately 25.6 percent of the total issued shares of Mid Ocean Limited.
